subject: general
question: Select the INCORRECT pair.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kulhad — non-biodegradable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kulhad** is a traditional clay cup commonly used in India for serving tea or other beverages.
 
• It is made from natural clay and is therefore **biodegradable**.
 
• Being biodegradable, kulhads can decompose naturally over time and do not harm the environment.
 
• This makes kulhads environmentally friendly compared to plastic or other non-biodegradable materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vegetable — biodegradable**__

 __
 
• **Vegetables** are organic matter and decompose naturally.
 
• They are classified as **biodegradable** because they break down through natural processes.
 
• This decomposition enriches the soil with nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Plastic glass — non-biodegradable**__
 __
 
• **Plastic glass** is made from synthetic materials.
 
• It is classified as **non-biodegradable** because it does not decompose naturally.
 
• Improper disposal can lead to environmental pollution.
 
 
 
• **Paper cup — biodegradable**__
 
 
• **Paper cups** are made from paper, which is a natural material.
 
• They are generally **biodegradable** and can decompose naturally.
 
• However, if coated with plastic, they may not be fully biodegradable.
